authentication: api_key query parameter, documented as REQUIRED ('Public Key of users'); a SAM.gov system account is needed to obtain one. No key was registered.
free_tier: free after registration; no anonymous access
rate_limits: UNKNOWN - the documentation page was read but the quota table was not extracted; the API was not called with a valid key
licence: US federal government work, public domain in the US (17 U.S.C. 105)
update_frequency: near real time for opportunity notices (documented); not verifiable without a key
historical_coverage: opportunity notices; the documentation notes date-range windows for public queries. Not verified live.
known_limitations: Registration required: the documentation marks api_key as mandatory. No key was created for this task, so no record was retrieved - REQUIRES_REGISTRATION is a documented plus observed-refusal conclusion, not a capability claim.

The live observation is weak on its own: both the key-less and the bogus-key request were answered by the istio-envoy gateway with HTTP 404 and an empty body, not 401/403. A 404 does not prove 'needs registration' by itself, which is why the register cites the documentation for that claim.
Opportunity notices are pre-award. They show demand and requirements, not awards or revenue; they must not be merged with award records.
No device identifier: the description is free text, so linking a notice to a specific product or model is not possible from structured fields.
The SAM.gov entity/bulk extract files (SAM Entity Management) are a separate, also account-gated mechanism and were not probed.
research_value: Would add the US pre-award stage (solicitations and sources-sought) to complement USAspending's post-award view, which is the missing first step of the procurement chain for the US. It is blocked only by a free registration, so it is a high-value, low-effort follow-up if an account is ever permitted.
cost_notes: free but account-gated; no payment required
